marquee.purpose: A film's name when it has no logo, empty-state headlines, and the handoff title. Wide and heavy.

title.purpose: Page titles and the compact hero title. At 460 condensed it sets the handoff signal slug.

heading.purpose: Wordmark, Play, list choices and handoff sub-lines.

notes.purpose: List details and the handoff's programme lines. Note badges use the badge size (1.25rem, 560, condensed).

body.purpose: Overviews (max 60ch), quiet actions and card titles.

caption.purpose: Episode codes, title counts, minutes left, server name.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked condensed word naming the value beside or below it: signal state words, station names, credit terms, field labels. Never decorative above a heading.

shadows.name: logo-lift
shadows.purpose: Keeps a film logo legible over a bright backdrop. Logos only.

shadows.name: sheet-edge
shadows.purpose: Separates the track side sheet from the page. Side sheet only.

shadows.purpose: The deeper ink field once focus moves into the programme rows.

motion.name: ease-curtain
motion.purpose: Focus scale, hero lift, ink field change and backdrop re-light.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: The house dimming during the screening handoff.

motion.name: focus
motion.purpose: The focus mark: paper ring plus scale to 1.06.

motion.name: relight
motion.purpose: Backdrop cross-fade when the featured or focused film changes.

motion.name: row-transition
motion.purpose: Rows passed fade out; waiting rows dim pictures to 50%.

motion.name: hero-hold
motion.purpose: The hero advances only after 20 s with no input; never under reduced motion. One paper rule across the content width, between the hero and the first row, fills over the hold; no preview of the next film.

motion.name: handoff
motion.purpose: Stations House, Programme, Picture, in that order.

narrative.overview:
Every screen is set like a page of a printed programme seen from the couch. The owner's own artwork is the ground: backdrops run full bleed and a deep warm near-black ink field rises over the lower part of the frame to carry the type. On that ink, one variable grotesk family does all the work by changing width: titles go wide and heavy, technical notes go condensed with tabular figures, and quiet badges, with each format's own logo, carry the facts under a title. Nothing is rounded, nothing floats on a card, and one red does all the colour work: it marks the section you are in and it fills the action that starts the film. Play is the only red block that carries a line of type.

The system is built for ten feet and a d-pad. The root size tracks the screen height (1rem is 100vh / 67.5, so 16px at 1080p and 32px at 4K), every layout sits inside a 5% overscan-safe frame, and every focusable thing shows focus by two cues at once. Motion is slow and theatrical (long eased re-lights, a dimming house before playback) and disappears entirely under reduced motion.

Density is low and deliberate. A screen carries one title, one line of programme notes, a few actions, and the top of the next row. Technical facts are stated plainly with their real signal state, never dressed as badges.
keyCharacteristics: Artwork as the ground, a warm near-black ink field as the reading surface.
One variable family, hierarchy carried by width (62 to 125 axis) as much as weight.
Square geometry throughout; hairline rules instead of containers.
One accent, Harakiri Red, a dark arterial red: it fills Play and Resume and marks sections with short tabs. Play is the only red block that carries horizontal type.
Problems carry a small Torch Amber square and words, never red, so an error is never read as the brand.
Focus is a paper outline plus scale, or a full paper inversion, never colour alone.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Harakiri Red is the only saturated surface in the product; Torch Amber appears only as a small problem mark. The red has two jobs. It names where you are: the margin's section tab, the short tab before each row and sheet head, the Welcome band, the selected season's underline, and text selection. It starts the film: the Play and Resume fill, and the player's state tile, Play in miniature. No other control, badge, focus state, fact or illustration may use it.

rules.name: The Red Names Or Starts Rule
rules.body: Only Play and Resume are red blocks that carry a line of type, so a red block with words on it always starts the film. Section names sit in paper on ink beside a red tab, or run upward in the margin's tab. Tabs, bands and the season underline are never focusable, and the underline says which season is showing, not where focus is. The player's state tile shows whether the film that started is playing or paused; it is not a control. Focus on red is the paper ring and scale, never a change of red.

rules.name: The Problem Is Never Red Rule
rules.body: Every problem leads with the Torch Amber square, the height of a capital, and states itself in plain words at weight 560. That covers a section that did not load, a wrong password, an unreachable server, a failed start, a server transcode, and a downgrade in the player. Red stays the brand's, so a band never reads as an alarm and an alarm never reads as a band.

rules.name: The Paper On Ink Rule
rules.body: Type is paper on ink at three strengths (paper, dim, faint). Hue is never used to rank text.

rules.name: The Width Carries Rank Rule
rules.body: Wide means a name, condensed means a fact. Titles and section names set wide (118 to 125%); notes, numbers and captions set condensed (72%); running copy sits at 86 to 100%.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular across the whole product, set on the body. Do not switch to proportional figures for display.

rules.name: The Ink Field Rule
rules.body: Type over artwork always sits on the graded ink field. Never place type on a raw backdrop, and never use a hard stop: the ramp is eased so bright skies fade into ink without a horizon line.

dos: Do size everything in rem so it scales with screen height (1rem is 100vh / 67.5), and keep content inside the 5vw by 5vh safe frame.
Do show focus with two cues: the paper outline with scale, or a full paper inversion. Never only a colour change.
Do set names wide (118 to 125%) and facts condensed (72%) with tabular figures.
Do mark signal state by shape plus word: solid square native, half square mapped, outline square decoded.
Do put type over artwork only on the eased ink field.
Do dim only the pictures of inactive rows; keep their type at full contrast.
Do keep the handoff stations in order: House, then Programme, then Picture.
Do respect reduced motion: no auto-advancing hero, no transitions.
donts: Don't use Harakiri Red for anything but the section tab on Settings and onboarding, the tab before row and sheet heads, the Welcome band, the selected season's underline, text selection, the Play and Resume fill, and the player's state tile.
Don't set a line of type on a red block other than Play and Resume, make a tab or band focusable, or show focus by changing the red; focus on red is the paper ring and scale.
Don't run the margin band the full height of the screen; it is a tab as tall as its section name. Only Welcome runs it full height.
Don't round corners or put titles on floating cards.
Don't use colour alone to carry focus, state or errors.
Don't use red for errors or warnings; problems carry the Torch Amber square and words.
Don't advance the hero while the owner is pressing, or at all under reduced motion.
Don't add shadows beyond the logo lift and the sheet edge.
Don't set an uppercase tracked label above a heading as decoration; labels only name the value beside or below them.
Don't use the film the product is named after, or its imagery, as decoration.
Don't turn the red into blood imagery: no drips, splatter or wounds. It is a colour, not a motif.
